summary: M.S. in Computer Engineering from Rochester Institute of Technology. I take computer vision models from raw sensor data to deployed inference: curating and generating training datasets, training detection and segmentation models in PyTorch, and optimizing them with TensorRT and 8-bit quantization for NVIDIA Jetson edge hardware. My work spans classical computer vision through custom models trained on vehicle and lane-marking data.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Curated and annotated a custom object detection dataset for health-level classification, owning the data from collection through model handoff.
Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 images to 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for on-device inference.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a metal surface inspection pipeline for microscopic crack analysis using custom image stitching, wavelet denoising, and depth estimation.

Designed an alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5 wavelet bank with optimized homography stitching to reach a PSNR of 86 against a 65 baseline; deployed ZoeDepth depth estimation for crack profiling at +/-8% error.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Engineered custom data and training pipelines for the BraTS 2020 multi-modal dataset with augmentation and batch-loading memory management for large 3D inputs.
Trained U-Net segmentation with VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-50 backbones; evaluated on Dice Score and IoU and reported accuracy-latency trade-offs for deployment.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving Perception Stack (CARLA)
bullets: Built automated data generation pipelines using semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering to produce ~8,000 detection and lane training frames with zero manual annotation.
Trained YOLO11n (mAP50 ~0.85) for vehicle detection and fine-tuned UFLD (ResNet-18) for lane-marking segmentation; drove Town02 collision-free.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Deployed TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing on NVIDIA Jetson, achieving a 5.2x inference speedup (56.7 to 10.9 ms, 17.6 to 92 FPS) over eager PyTorch.
Built a multiprocessing multi-camera data collection pipeline feeding a three-layer distributed system over a WebSocket fabric.
Debugged 11 integration failures in physical operation (false positives, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to reach 100% pick reliability across 10 trials.

projects.name: Model Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Cut GPU memory footprint ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8) and profiled peak VRAM and inference latency with pynvml.
Benchmarked across HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC at under 1% accuracy degradation, quantifying the efficiency-versus-accuracy trade-off for edge deployment.
